neighbours.label: a preposition (with/from/upon) whose object is about to be a government or state
fire: The opposition party demanded answers from the Kenyan government.
After years of tension, Cuba restored ties with Washington.
The charity appealed to the national authorities for more funding.
Unions called upon the Prime Minister to raise the minimum wage.
Farmers sought compensation from the provincial government.
The rebels signed a ceasefire with the military junta.
Human rights groups urged pressure on the Iranian regime.
Exporters asked for support from the European Commission.
quiet: The opposition party ordered pizza from the corner shop.
After years of tension, the brothers restored ties with each other.
The charity appealed to local bakers for more bread.
Unions called upon their members to bring snacks to the picnic.
Farmers bought fresh seed from the village market.
The children built a fort with the old cardboard boxes.
Teachers urged pressure on the faucet to stop the leak.
Exporters asked for advice from their accountants.

notes: Top examples: 'rapprochement with the United States', 'action on housing from the Haitian government', 'called upon the United States'. Output suppresses ' government' (predicting it). Probe: 'negotiate with the Syrian government' 0.40, 'aid from the federal authorities' 0.48; non-political 'with'/'from' ~0.01-0.03.
